reason: This text (Job 1:1-22) is not structured around a contrast between right leaders and wrong regular people. Instead, it focuses on introducing Job as a righteous patriarch (described as 'blameless, upright, fearing God') and depicting his faithful response to calamities. While Job does worry that his sons may have sinned and offers sacrifices on their behalf, this concern about potential sin is not the narrative's main point. The passage emphasizes Job's own righteousness and his acceptance of God's will despite losing everything. The central theme is Job's virtue being tested by Satan, not an exposition of leaders being right versus regular people being wrong. The narrative structure is one of theodicy and faithfulness under trial, not of moral hierarchy between leadership classes.
